sources.supports: Log-buffer waits, clean-page waits, effective resized capacity, current/checkpoint LSN and logical redo range have different meanings.
Redo management/capacity and checkpoint behavior, preserving measured burst/drain interpretation.
8.4 changed adaptive hash, change buffering, Linux flush method and I/O defaults; actual configuration still matters.
Deadlock rolls back entire transaction; default lock-wait timeout rolls back the waiting statement.
Found unique record exception, RC constraint-check gaps, snapshot and row-based binlog consequences.
Relay-log flush before acknowledgement, no required completed apply, timeout fallback and selectable wait point.
Online ALTER still needs exclusive metadata locking; pending exclusive request can block later queries.
Server cursor materializes results and does not promise bounded server memory or streaming query execution.
lock_wait_timeout applies separately to metadata-lock acquisitions, not total DDL duration.
Connector/J 8.4.0 executeBatchWithMultiValuesClause, lines 647–753: more than one entry receives 0 for zero total or SUCCESS_NO_INFO otherwise on successful path.
Connector/J 8.4.0 lines 59–61 enables server preparation when cursor fetching is enabled.
Connector/J 8.4.0 lines 604–606 row-streaming eligibility and 2086–2089 cursor-fetch eligibility.
Connector/J 8.4.0 lines 103–118 close drains unread records.
INSTANT permits only LOCK=DEFAULT; INPLACE/online does not imply no rebuild or metadata-lock requirement.
EXPLAIN ANALYZE executes supported statements; iterator time includes children and is average per loop.
